exposure: maternal perception of reduced fetal movements
outcome: Cesarean delivery due to non-reassuring fetal heart rate monitoring
cohort: 203 term pregnancies with RFM during the 2 weeks prior to delivery, matched with 203 controls
finding: After excluding important placental-related morbidities, RFM was associated with a higher rate of placental weight <10th percentile and placental maternal vascular malperfusion lesions compared to controls.
mod_finding: The reduced fetal movement group had higher rates of cesarean delivery due to non-reassuring fetal heart rate monitoring.
